transcript.text: My fridge freezer has been making a funny smell in the kitchen the last couple of days, I've cleaned it out but it's still there. Any ideas?

Yes — after the inside has been cleaned, the common cause is stagnant defrost water or debris in the drain/drip tray, but the type of smell matters. If it is hot plastic or burning, switch it off and unplug it now and do not keep using it; that needs an engineer. A sour, musty or dirty-water smell is more consistent with the drain or tray, while a sharp chemical smell or loss of cooling needs prompt professional attention.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Oh dear, it does smell like hot plastic, a bit electrical, and it's stronger round the back than inside. There's been an occasional buzzing from the back too, and the plug feels a little warm. Should I switch it off at the wall now?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Yes — switch it off at the wall now, then unplug it if the plug can be removed without touching anything hot or damaged. Do not use it again until a qualified appliance engineer/electrician has checked it. A hot-plastic/electrical smell from the rear plus a warm plug points to an overheating electrical connection, lead/plug/socket, or possibly the compressor start components; the buzzing may be related but cannot identify the failed part safely. If there is any browning, melting or scorching at the plug or socket, leave it isolated and arrange an electrician as well as an appliance engineer.

candidates: Stagnant water or debris in the defrost drain/drip tray (medium)
Electrical overheating at the plug, wiring or compressor area (low)
Food residue or a spill outside the cleaned compartments (medium)

reading.symptom: funny smell coming from the fridge freezer

plan: They asked: "Any ideas?" - answer that first.
Checks they have done and what they found: cleaned out the fridge freezer - smell is still there.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell coming from the fridge freezer". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.

Compressor start relay/overload or compressor electrical fault (medium)
